creator: bengusberg
title: Four-agent dev team in Claude Cowork (Architect, Coder, Tester, Manager); give them one small product and review like a CEO

tools.name: Claude Cowork
tools.detail: Prompt typed in Cowork tab: 'Create 4 agents wi...'; UI shows Chat | Cowork toggle, 'Project or folder', 'Manual' mode

claims: Creator is a Stanford founder of an AI startup that has raised $4 million
Uses four Claude agents as his personal dev team
Agents 'tend to argue with each other, but that's the point'
You don't need to review the code, only know your customer and whether the output is right
how_to_steps: Step 1: open Claude Cowork and prompt 'create four agents with these specific job descriptions': Agent 1 Architect (turns ideas into a build plan, asks key questions first); Agent 2 Coder (writes code from the plan); Agent 3 Tester (only job is breaking what the coder builds); Agent 4 Manager (reviews the others' work and flags key issues to you)
Step 2: give the team one small product (a waitlist page or an internal tool), not a big idea
Step 3: review the output like a CEO — say what is wrong, let them fix it, iterate
on_screen_only: Pixel-art cards labeled Architect, Coder, Tester, Manager
Cowork input box with partially typed 'ate 4 agents wi' and suggestions 'Send me a daily briefing', 'Organize my inbox'
Captions: 'WE'VE RAISED $4 MILLION', 'CREATE FOUR AGENTS', 'WAIT LIST PAGE'
cta: Try it and tell him what your team ships; follow for AI founder content

relevance.why: Simple framing of role-split subagents that a solo founder can map onto Claude Code subagents (planner / implementer / tester / reviewer); the 'review as CEO, not as a code reviewer' advice fits a time-poor builder.

implement_score.why: Trivial to define as four Claude Code subagents or Cowork agents in 15 minutes; the real value is the tester/reviewer roles. Scored 3 not higher because the video offers no evidence it beats a single agent plus a review pass.

verify: Does Claude Cowork actually support persistent named agents from one prompt, or is this just a role-play prompt?
Token/cost overhead of four agents vs one agent with plan/test/review phases
Whether the 'you don't need to review the code' advice is safe for anything beyond a waitlist page
